observation: The whole set in the opening position, and it reads as one object. TOP: the four dark_gray panels butt into one board with no seam gap and no overlap; the twelve cocoa_brown belt tiles sit as two 3x2 blocks either side of the centre line, all twelve flush in their pockets and none proud of the field; the black Anti-Sol den sits at the far mid-line with three cyan corona cells around it (one each side, one in front) and the beige Sol den at the near mid-line with three orange ones, which is three traps per den exactly as the source game wants; eight black-disc worlds stand across the far three ranks and eight white-disc worlds across the near three, one per cell, none straddling a cell boundary and no two discs overlapping. The two gray trays lie off the board with eight scooped sockets each, eight per army. ISO: the size ladder reads straight off the picture -- the two largest globes are the banded orange pair, then the two ringed worlds, then the blues, down to the small gray and the small red -- and every globe sits concentric on its own disc with its seat collar covered. Nothing intersects anything: no globe touches its neighbour, no ring touches a disc or the board, no belt tile rides up on a panel edge. The only things standing proud of the playing field are the four den flames, two per star, which is the one raised vocabulary this edition allows; every corona cell is flat with its sunburst cut INTO the top face, and no trap tile carries anything above its face at any corner. FRONT: one silhouette at bed level, every disc bottom on the same line, the globes graded in height across the rank, and the two den flames the only things breaking the skyline. The two trays read as floating because this renderer draws no ground plane and casts no shadow; that is a property of the picture, not of the solids. No misplaced, missing or extra parts, no proportion or size mismatch, no visible intersection, no floating geometry in the set itself.
